title: Basis for the Co-Payment Collected on a Cabin Move — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
A move into a higher cabin is sold only on an Air Ticket Fare Brands brand that allows it, at that brand's co-payment for each traveller counted into the move and for each segment the move is taken over, and the booking is never converted to the higher cabin's own brand terms.

## 1. The travellers counted into the move

The co-payment for moving into a higher cabin is worked out only after the booking's lines carry the agency service charge owed for every traveller the booking carries, and until that charge is complete only the travellers whose places the standing lines already cover are counted into the move.

Those lines carry that charge for every traveller the booking carries only where they come to at least the fare brand's own agency service fee taken once for each of them; short of that they carry it for as many travellers as there are such lines.

## 2. The remaining quantities

2.1 **The brand's co-payment.** The upgrade co-payment scheduled for the fare brand the booking is held in, taken per traveller per segment.
2.2 **The segments moved.** The move is taken over 1 segment.
2.3 **The programme discount.** No programme discount is taken off the gross co-payment: the discount stands at 0 percent.
2.4 **The lead-time share.** The late share of that figure is carried forward: 1.15 of it.
2.5 **The credit for extras already bought.** No credit is given for optional extras already bought: the credit stands at 0.00 USD.
2.6 **The approval share.** The unapproved share of what is left is carried forward: 0.85, being 85 percent.
2.7 **The traveller's own share.** The whole of the figure is collected from the traveller: a share of 1.

## 3. The order the operations take

The brand's co-payment, the travellers counted and the segments the move is taken over are multiplied together into the gross co-payment; the programme discount acts on that gross figure, the lead-time share acts on the result of that step, the credit for extras already bought is taken off the result of that second step, the approval share acts on what is left, and the traveller's own share acts last.

The co-payment collected never falls below zero, and the result is rounded to the nearest cent.

## 4. Worked figure, on hypothetical inputs

A booking carrying 2 travellers whose agency service lines come to 49.90 USD against a brand whose agency service fee is a hypothetical 24.95 USD, held in a brand whose upgrade co-payment is a hypothetical 300.00 USD.

| Step | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| the service lines of 49.90 USD come to at least 24.95 USD taken once for each of 2 travellers, so the travellers counted are | 2 |
| the co-payment of 300.00 USD, the 2 travellers counted and the 1 segment multiplied together | 600.00 USD |
| the programme discount of 0 percent acting on the gross co-payment | 600.00 USD |
| the lead-time share of 1.15 acting on that result | 690.00 USD |
| the credit of 0.00 USD taken off that second result | 690.00 USD |
| the approval share of 0.85 acting on what is left | 586.50 USD |
| the traveller's own share of 1 acting last | 586.50 USD |
| held at nothing were it lower, and rounded to the nearest cent | 586.50 USD |

Were the same booking to carry only 1 agency service line of 24.95 USD against its 2 travellers, the lines would fall short of 24.95 USD taken once for each of them, and the travellers counted would be the 1 such line, giving a gross co-payment of 300.00 USD and a figure of 293.25 USD.
